newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mostly up on rebound.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Monday on a technical rebound after continued losses over the past few trading days, traders said.

The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,298 yuan ($398) per tonne, unchanged from Friday's close. It opened at 3,295 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 3,294 and a high of 3,299 yuan per tonne.
July rose 26 to 3,280 yuan per tonne, November four to 3,298 and the January 1998 contract 65 to 3,298 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 19,100 tonnes from 18,800 tonnes.
Soybeans opened higher and rose steadily for most of the session, traders said.

"Speculative players took advantage of technical overselling to push prices up today," one trader said. "But the upward potential will be limited because most investors believe the current price levels are reasonable."
Traders said they expected soybeans to linger around the 3,300 yuan level for the next few days.
